# S1 — Isolate review-gate scratch on a dedicated EBS volume

## Why
Review gate scratch/clones/snapshots currently share the OS/root filesystem. A burst or leak in review work can therefore wedge the whole Gerrit host. Option C is the walking-skeleton structural fix: move gate scratch to a separately sized/quota'd EBS volume.

## What
Add a dedicated gp3 EBS volume for code-review gate scratch, mount it at a documented host path such as `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`, and wire review-bot temp handling so both `rebar-gate-snapshots` and `reviewbot-*` clone workdirs use that filesystem. Reuse the existing Nitro NVMe-by-volume-id mount pattern from `infra/terraform/user_data.sh:20-70`. Add a scratch-volume metric and CloudWatch alarm.

## Scope
In scope: Terraform volume/attachment/variables/outputs, user-data mount, review-bot compose env/mounts, observability metric, CloudWatch alarm, runbook updates, and targeted tests. Out of scope: Docker/Journald/`/var/tmp`/container-layer caps; those depend on this structural slice.

## Grounding
- Existing data EBS volume and attachment: `infra/terraform/main.tf:27-35`, `:83-87`.
- Root block device and user-data render: `infra/terraform/main.tf:56-64`; variables: `infra/terraform/variables.tf:13-23`.
- Current scratch is root-resident because `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` is unset: `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:233-245`, `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:149-163`, `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:381`, `src/rebar/review_bot/low_disk.py:69`.
- Runbook states clone workdirs are root-volume resident: `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:575-606`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Terraform declares a separate scratch EBS volume, attachment, size/cap variables, tags, and outputs; scratch is documented as rebuildable rather than source-of-truth data.
- [ ] Host provisioning mounts the scratch volume idempotently by UUID and fails loud if it cannot mount.
- [ ] Review-bot snapshot store and clone tempdirs resolve to the scratch volume, not root.
- [ ] Scratch volume publishes a metric and has its own CloudWatch alarm wired to SNS.
- [ ] Runbooks document steady-state location, alarm meaning, recovery, and rebuildable-data posture.
- [ ] Targeted tests cover Terraform alarm/action conventions, compose/env wiring, and observability emission.
- [ ] Portability criterion: control is Terraform + Linux mount/env config with local tests; no GitHub-only CI trigger is required.
